### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **135** documentable anchor(s).

**49** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (6 routes)`, `packageId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`, `/api/v1/meta (route, 42 pages)`
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7007b4e6d9294b466b0805cae72ef81fee99fa3b` — the merge of head `7e12df4c01dec7a8e33bf0c4e7c2f318a9d9ac2b` into base `a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7007b4e6d9294b466b0805cae72ef81fee99fa3b && git checkout 7007b4e6d9294b466b0805cae72ef81fee99fa3b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a 7e12df4c01dec7a8e33bf0c4e7c2f318a9d9ac2b && git checkout -B drift-repro a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a && git merge --no-ff 7e12df4c01dec7a8e33bf0c4e7c2f318a9d9ac2b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a285ff29a18ac6ae2a9a72943f58733ce31f299a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `7e12df4c01dec7a8e33bf0c4e7c2f318a9d9ac2b`
Local-runs: none

The face is the declaration face. This review is owed only by `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` on the plugin-security changeset and the PR body. The tree carries no published schema and no governed path (`check-governed-merges --pr 25512`: 0 of 5 paths), and no narrowing is declared. The lane seat renders it as its review of record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The new boot report `upgrade-impact-report.ts` is a widening of what an operator is told, and it is right.**
   - It reads the activation ledger, `sys_metadata`, `sys_webhook`, the object rows, extensions, navigation diagnostics and the setting keys, and it compares them against the registry.
   - It writes no row and refuses no operation. The unit pin asserts that no write verb is ever requested.
   - Item 2 and item 4 of ruling 6259332195 ask for this report. It reuses the access report's delivery and posture rules, with no new door.
2. **The new notification topic `system.upgrade_impact` is right.**
   - It is emitted through the existing `messaging.emit()` ingress, using the #25489 delivery helper.
   - Its `dedupKey` is computed over the sorted finding set, so a repeat boot is skipped. R5 shows one row, then "already emitted; skipping".
   - Under a wall it follows #25489 exactly: the operator line, plus an in-app copy only in the organization that `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_ORGANIZATION` names.
3. **Settings are read by key and never by value: right.** The scan does not select the value column. The R5 defect, where the core logger redacted a field named `key`, is fixed by naming it `name`, and a real-logger replay case pins that.
4. **The stops are right.** An unreadable store or unreadable settings manifests stop the report for that boot with one `warn`. An unread answer is never taken as "resolves nowhere", so no false finding is raised.
5. **The public surface is unchanged.**
   - The new module's exports (`UPGRADE_IMPACT_TOPIC`, the type lists, `SETTINGS_SERVICE` and others) are module-level only.
   - plugin-security's `index.ts` is not in the diff.
   - `security-plugin.ts` gains one import and one guarded call in `kernel:bootstrapped`. The call has its own `try`/`catch`, so a failure cannot break the access report or the boot. The `ql as any` argument matches the neighbouring `reportAccessUpgrade` call.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-security` ships `patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the body.
- AGENTS.md says a non-protocol change ships `patch`, widening or breaking. A notification topic and log lines are not authorable metadata, so `none` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Card relation:** the PR body says `Part of #24447`. The spec half, retiring `packages/spec/src/kernel/package-upgrade.zod.ts` with its ADR-0087 conversion, belongs to the spec lane. It has been asked for in 6367978063 and in pointer 6367986096 on #18549, and it has no card yet. The two halves have no ordering between them.
- **Concurrent edit:** draft #25516 (#25223 split, row 8) also edits `security-plugin.ts`. A pairwise `git merge-tree` of the two heads is clean, and this PR's hunk is a pure addition inside `kernel:bootstrapped`, which that cut does not move. Whichever lands second merges `main`, and the split cut re-proves its `.d.ts` on its own new base.
- **Not judged, on purpose:** ADR-0005's package-less overlay, rows bound to authored, unknown or disabled packages, unregistered settings namespaces, and contributions to missing apps. All of these are named in the module header. Accepted as scope.
- **Dev flags:** the report lists no `open_questions` and no out-of-scope findings.
- **Evidence:**
  - 39 + 5 cases.
  - 6 ablations turn 5, 5, 1, 5, 4 and 4 red, and each restore is clean.
  - plugin-security: 4529 passed.
  - dispatch-gates: 69/69.
  - R5 production `os serve` under `single` and `isolated`, with the setting both unset and set.
  - CI on this head: 39 success, 9 skipped.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mfvys8`
Reviewed-by: `session_016g7nYP9wdNx1GDa5XDr7Uy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
